description: Camera comparison: near 6%, standard 5%, far 4%; four layouts and two encounter densities. Version 1 failed its three-image open-oval pilot; version 2 moves camera instructions first and pilots staggered plinths before any batch. All failures retained.
common: Use case: stylized-concept. Original Roman-era elemental-mage arena, Tessera & Lime palette: chalk sand, terracotta, mineral blue, umber contour. Hand-painted digital overhead map with small edge tesserae and matte pigment. Do not depict an ancient wall mural: depict a playable arena seen from high above. No text, UI, letters, logos or photorealism.

items.prompt: EXTREME LONG SHOT, HIGH AERIAL VIEW. Landscape arena floor fills the entire 16:9 image. The camera is 55 degrees above the ground. Tiny overhead people with the tops of their heads visible, each whole person 5% of image height (36 pixels at 720p). The distant people look like tiny specks on a huge map: no faces or anatomy details. Vast empty floor separates every person. No large person, no foreground person. An enormous open sand-and-lime oval. Only a fragment of its distant boundary at the very top; floor continues outside the other three edges. No enclosing postcard frame. One tiny blue mage near centre and four tiny ochre/red enemies spaced widely, with clear escape paths between. A little cyan open crescent immediately in front of the blue mage, facing one incoming red projectile; the back of the mage is open. Two hollow red floor warning circles twice the height of a person. One thin blue bolt. The setting and immense ground area dominate; people are miniature accents.
